plan.title: Sesiidae homework: when does molecular electronics explain biological specificity?

acts.title: What the head group does
acts.predict: Where is each molecule most electron-rich? Which has an H-bond donor? Does adding the acetyl make "everything more negative"?
tasks: Identify the largest electrostatic differences between the three head groups and explain them with ordinary organic chemistry: electronegativity, resonance in the ester, donor and acceptor.
Explore how far the head-group perturbation appears to extend, with the difference card. These chain-site comparisons are descriptive and exploratory, not a prespecified test.
acts.expected: This act is the "ESP works" act. Global V_max: resolved, the prespecified result.

blocks.label: S. tenuis gland, Japan and Korea

acts.title: What E/Z does (E3 vs Z3 acetate)
acts.predict: Does changing E to Z at C3 mainly change the charge distribution, or the shape?
tasks: Read the difference card at C3-H, C4-H and head O. Is each difference larger than that site's conformer range? Than its partition sensitivity?
Look at the extended and folded conformers of one compound side by side, on the same scale.
acts.expected: E/Z is not resolved at any site. C3-H: different on average.

acts.title: Where the double bond is (E2 vs E3 acetate)
acts.predict: Moving C=C by one carbon. Which sites should change, and by how much compared with act B?
tasks: Compare C2-H, C3-H and C4-H between the two compounds, with the difference card. Which differences exceed the conformer range?
Does free-molecule ESP give a convincing reason an organism or enzyme would treat these two compounds differently?
acts.expected: Resolved at C4 only. Question 2's honest answer stays no.

acts.title: What is missing
acts.predict: The organism makes, or responds to, one particular compound. Suppose free-molecule ESP does not explain the distinction. What information is missing, and how would you get it?
acts.expected: The receptor's or enzyme's geometry, active-site residues, orientation, dynamics, and experimental evidence.
